# Introduction

The purpose of this simulation study is to investigate the statistical

behaviour of different bandwidth-selection methods for kernel density

estimation using the Epanechnikov kernel.

We compare three bandwidth selectors:

1. an AMISE plug-in estimator,

2. likelihood cross-validation,

3. least-squares cross-validation (LSCV).

Because the true density is known in simulation, the selected bandwidths

can also be compared with a sample-specific oracle bandwidth that minimizes

the integrated squared error (ISE).

The simulations consider distributions with different characteristics:

- a smooth symmetric normal density,

- a skewed Gamma density,

- a multimodal Gaussian mixture.

This allows us to study how the methods respond to different underlying

density shapes.

# Background

## Kernel density estimation

Given observations $X_1,\ldots,X_N$, the kernel density estimator is

$$
\hat f_h(x) = \frac{1}{Nh}\sum_{i=1}^N K\left(\frac{x-X_i}{h}\right).
$$

We use the Epanechnikov kernel,

$$
K(u) = \frac34(1-u^2)\mathbf{1}_{\{|u|\leq1\}}.
$$

The bandwidth $h>0$ controls the bias–variance trade-off. Its mean integrated squared error (MISE) is

$$
\operatorname{MISE}(h) = \int \operatorname{Var}\{\hat f_h(x)\}\,dx
+ \int \operatorname{Bias}\{\hat f_h(x)\}^2\,dx.
$$

Smaller bandwidths typically reduce bias but increase variance, while larger bandwidths smooth more aggressively.

## AMISE plug-in selection

Assuming sufficient smoothness of the true density $f_0$, the asymptotic mean integrated squared error is

$$
\operatorname{AMISE}(h) = \frac{\|K\|_2^2}{Nh}
+ \frac{h^4\sigma_K^4}{4}\|f_0''\|_2^2,
$$

where $\sigma_K^2=\int u^2K(u)\,du$. For the Epanechnikov kernel,

$$
\|K\|_2^2 = \frac35, \qquad \sigma_K^2 = \frac15.
$$

Minimizing AMISE with respect to $h$ yields

$$
h_{\mathrm{AMISE}} =
\left(\frac{\|K\|_2^2}{N\sigma_K^4\|f_0''\|_2^2}\right)^{1/5}.
$$

Since $f_0''$ is unknown, we replace its integrated squared norm with an estimate based on a pilot Gaussian kernel density estimate $\tilde f_r$. Specifically,

$$
\|\tilde f_r''\|_2^2 = \frac{1}{N^2r^6}
\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{j=1}^N
\int H''\left(\frac{x-X_i}{r}\right)
H''\left(\frac{x-X_j}{r}\right)\,dx.
$$

We choose the pilot bandwidth using a Silverman-type rule, $r=0.9\tilde\sigma N^{-1/5}$, where $\tilde\sigma$ denotes the scale estimate used in the implementation.

For efficiency, the Gaussian pilot can also be evaluated via the closed-form derivative convolution. Writing $\phi$ for the standard normal density and $d=(X_i-X_j)/r$,

$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\phi''(u)\phi''(u+d)\,du
= \frac{d^4-12d^2+12}{32\sqrt\pi}\exp(-d^2/4).
$$

We compare the pilot calculation approaches in the implementation where relevant.

## Cross-validation

For likelihood cross-validation, observations are divided into $k$ folds. Let $F(i)$ denote the fold containing observation $i$, and let $T_i=\{j:j\notin F(i)\}$ be its training indices. The training-sample density estimate is

$$
\hat f_{h,-F(i)}(x) = \frac{1}{|T_i|h}
\sum_{j\in T_i}K\left(\frac{x-X_j}{h}\right).
$$

The log-likelihood score and selected bandwidth are

$$
\ell_{\mathrm{CV}}(h) = \sum_{i=1}^N
\log\hat f_{h,-F(i)}(X_i), \qquad
h_{\mathrm{loglik}} = \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{h}\ell_{\mathrm{CV}}(h).
$$

Least-squares cross-validation (LSCV) instead minimizes an empirical approximation to integrated squared error. Using the leave-one-out estimate $\hat f_{h,-i}$,

$$
\operatorname{LSCV}(h) =
\int \hat f_h(x)^2\,dx
-\frac{2}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\hat f_{h,-i}(X_i), \qquad
h_{\mathrm{LSCV}}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_h\operatorname{LSCV}(h).
$$

The integral can be approximated numerically using the trapezoidal rule, as implemented in the accompanying R functions. Likelihood CV is maximized, whereas LSCV is minimized.

```{r}
#| label: cv-objective-data
x_cv <- mixture_example$sample
h_grid_cv <- seq(
  0.05,
  2,
  length.out = 80
)
set.seed(100)
fold_id <- make_folds(
  x_cv,
  k = 5
)
loglik_scores <- vapply(
  h_grid_cv,
  function(h) {
    cv_loglik_score(
      x = x_cv,
      h = h,
      fold_id = fold_id
    )
  },
  numeric(1)
)
lscv_scores <- vapply(
  h_grid_cv,
  function(h) {
    lscv_score(
      x = x_cv,
      h = h
    )
  },
  numeric(1)
)
h_loglik <- h_grid_cv[
  which.max(loglik_scores)
]
h_lscv <- h_grid_cv[
  which.min(lscv_scores)
]
loglik_data <- data.frame(
  bandwidth = h_grid_cv,
  score = loglik_scores
)
lscv_data <- data.frame(
  bandwidth = h_grid_cv,
  score = lscv_scores
)
```


```{r}
#| label: simulation-study
#| cache: false
B <- 50
n_sim <- 100
set.seed(1001)
normal_results <- run_simulation(
  scenario = scenarios$normal,
  n = n_sim,
  h_grid = seq(
    0.05,
    1.5,
    length.out = 40
  ),
  B = B,
  repeats = 3
)
normal_results$scenario <- "Normal"
set.seed(1002)
gamma_results <- run_simulation(
  scenario = scenarios$gamma,
  n = n_sim,
  h_grid = seq(
    0.05,
    1.5,
    length.out = 40
  ),
  B = B,
  repeats = 3
)
gamma_results$scenario <- "Gamma"
set.seed(1003)
mixture_results <- run_simulation(
  scenario = scenarios$mixture,
  n = n_sim,
  h_grid = seq(
    0.05,
    2,
    length.out = 40
  ),
  B = B,
  repeats = 3
)
mixture_results$scenario <- "Mixture"
all_results <- rbind(
  normal_results,
  gamma_results,
  mixture_results
)
```

```{r}
#| label: oracle-comparison-data
add_oracle_comparison <- function(results) {
  oracle_results <- subset(
    results,
    method == "Oracle",
    select = c(
      replicate,
      n,
      scenario,
      bandwidth,
      ise
    )
  )
  names(oracle_results)[
    names(oracle_results) == "bandwidth"
  ] <- "oracle_bandwidth"
  names(oracle_results)[
    names(oracle_results) == "ise"
  ] <- "oracle_ise"
  comparison <- merge(
    subset(
      results,
      method != "Oracle"
    ),
    oracle_results,
    by = c(
      "replicate",
      "n",
      "scenario"
    )
  )
  comparison$bandwidth_ratio <-
    comparison$bandwidth /
    comparison$oracle_bandwidth
  comparison$ise_ratio <-
    comparison$ise /
    comparison$oracle_ise
  comparison
}
oracle_comparison <- add_oracle_comparison(
  all_results
)
```

```{r}

print(p_oracle_bandwidth)
```

```{r}
#| label: sample-size-study
#| cache: true
n_values <- c(
  50,
  100,
  500
)
B_n <- 50
sample_size_results_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(n_values)
)
for (i in seq_along(n_values)) {
  set.seed(
    2000 + i
  )
  n_current <- n_values[i]
  result <- run_simulation(
    scenario = scenarios$mixture,
    n = n_current,
    h_grid = seq(
      0.05,
      2,
      length.out = 40
    ),
    B = B_n,
    repeats = 3
  )
  result$scenario <- "Mixture"
  sample_size_results_list[[i]] <- result
}
sample_size_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  sample_size_results_list
)
```

# Real-data example

The simulation study allows direct evaluation against a known density.

For real data the true density is unavailable, so performance cannot be

measured using ISE.

Instead, the bandwidth selectors are compared visually on the eruption

durations from the `faithful` dataset.

```{r}
#| label: faithful-data-summary
x_real <- datasets::faithful$eruptions
summary(x_real)
```

```{r}
#| label: faithful-bandwidths
h_grid_real <- seq(
  0.05,
  1.5,
  length.out = 80
)
set.seed(2026)
h_amise_real <- amise_bandwidth(
  x_real
)
loglik_real <- repeated_cv_loglik(
  x = x_real,
  h_grid = h_grid_real,
  k = 5,
  repeats = 10
)
lscv_real <- lscv_bandwidth(
  x = x_real,
  h_grid = h_grid_real
)
bandwidths_real <- c(
  AMISE = h_amise_real,
  LogLik_CV = loglik_real$bandwidth,
  LSCV = lscv_real$bandwidth
)
bandwidths_real
```

```{r}
#| label: faithful-density-data
grid_real <- seq(
  min(x_real) - max(bandwidths_real),
  max(x_real) + max(bandwidths_real),
  length.out = 1000
)
real_density_data <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    names(bandwidths_real),
    function(method) {
      data.frame(
        x = grid_real,
        density = kde_at(
          eval_points = grid_real,
          x = x_real,
          h = bandwidths_real[[method]]
        ),
        method = method
      )
    }
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: faithful-density-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
p_faithful <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(
    data = data.frame(x = x_real),
    aes(
      x = x,
      after_stat(density)
    ),
    bins = 25,
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = real_density_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = density,
      color = method
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Kernel density estimates for Old Faithful eruption durations",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "n = ",
      length(x_real)
    ),
    x = "Eruption duration (minutes)",
    y = "Density",
    color = "Bandwidth selector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
print(p_faithful)
#ggsave("plots/faithful_density.png", plot = p_faithful, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
)
```

## Comparison with reference R selectors

```{r}
#| label: reference-selector-comparison
selector_comparison <- run_selector_comparison(
  scenario = scenarios$mixture,
  B = 50,
  n = 200,
  h_grid = seq(
    0.05,
    2,
    length.out = 80
  ),
  k = 5,
  repeats = 3
)
```

```{r}
#| label: reference-selector-plots
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
plot_data <- subset(
  selector_comparison,
  method != "Oracle"
)
plot_data$source <- ifelse(
  grepl("^R_", plot_data$method),
  "R",
  "Own implementation"
)
p_bandwidth <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = method,
    y = bandwidth_ratio,
    fill = source
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.7,
    outlier.alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bandwidth selectors compared with the oracle",
    subtitle = "Gaussian mixture, n = 200, 50 simulations",
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(
      h[selector] / h[oracle]
    ),
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 25,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
p_ise <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = method,
    y = ise_ratio,
    fill = source
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.7,
    outlier.alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimation error relative to the oracle",
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(
      ISE / ISE[oracle]
    ),
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 25,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
p_selector_comparison <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  p_bandwidth,
  p_ise,
  nrow = 1,
  guides = "collect"
) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
print(p_selector_comparison)
#ggsave("plots/bandwidth_selection.png", plot = p_selector_comparison, width = 11, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```
